# Coverage wanted

<!-- Generated by scripts/coverage_wanted.py from data/coding_frame.csv, data/systems.json and schema/dimensions.json. Do not edit by hand; rerun the script. -->

HARNESS-DB codes 1,256 of the 6,504 systems in its sampling frame, on 38 dimensions (47,728 cells). This page lists where a contribution adds the most. To contribute, follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#add-or-update-a-system). To claim an item so two people do not code the same system, open an [add a system](https://github.com/harness-db/harness-db/issues/new?template=add_system.yml) issue first.

## 1. Systems in the frame that are not coded yet

The frame was coded as a stratified sample. Stratum H (high visibility) is coded completely; the other two were sampled:

| stratum | systems in frame | flagged coded |
|---|---:|---:|
| H | 984 | 984 |
| O | 4,837 | 100 |
| P | 683 | 150 |

5,247 frame systems are neither coded nor released. The 30 most-starred of them (by the star count recorded in the frame) are below. A contributed coding enters the next release as an unweighted addition: it was not drawn by the sample, so like the systems in section 3 it carries weight 0 in field-level estimates.

## 2. Dimensions where the sources are most often silent

A `not_reported` cell means the coder read the sources and they do not say. Evidence that settles one of these cells, a verbatim quote with a locator at a pinned commit, is the most useful single contribution: it is where the dataset is thinnest. Rate = `not_reported` / (cells - `unresolved`). The field-weighted rate (± design SE) uses the sampling weights and is the one the paper reports; the table is sorted by it.

## 3. Coded systems outside the stratified draw

23 released systems were coded for reasons other than the draw (several are benchmark reference agents, coded because the reference-set recall check needed them). They are in the release and count in every unweighted statement, but their inclusion probability is not the design one, so every field-level (weighted) estimate gives them weight 0. The stratum shown is the one the frame assigns; the draw did not select them.

What would help: an independent second reading of each, so that they can join the reliability sample, and reports of any cell that looks wrong.
